Name: Greece
Description: The land of Hellas, the Greek world whose people profile is the Greece entry in Ancient Civilizations, as distinct from its parts: the existing Achaia and Macedonia place entries are Roman-era regions within this larger land, not the whole of it. In Daniel, Greece appears in prophecy as the kingdom that would follow Persia, with its king named as the king of Grecia, and in Zechariah its sons stand for the Greek world opposed to God's people. By the time of Acts, Greece was the world Paul travelled through, preaching in its cities. This entry is the land as a whole, across both Testaments, rather than any one Greek city or province.
BiblicalSignificance: Greece matters in Scripture chiefly as the power that shaped the world between the Testaments: Daniel foresaw its empire, the Hellenistic age that followed spread the Greek language in which the New Testament was written, and Paul carried the gospel through its cities.
